{{Quote|The N-1 Starfighter represents the pinnacle in Naboo military technology. Armed with twin laser cannons and proton torpedoes, the agile N-1 is designed for patrol and escort missions. Deflector shields protect the pilot while an on-board astromech aids in navigation and repair.|[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo">''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]''</ref>}}
The [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] '''Royal N-1 starfighter''', sometimes known simply as the '''Naboo starfighter''', was a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] used by the government of Naboo during the late years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and early days of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] for defense, patrol, and escort duties. The sleek vessel was manufactured by [[Theed Palace Space Vessel Engineering Corps/Legends|Theed Palace Space Vessel Engineering Corps]], the group responsible for manufacturing Naboo royal [[Starship/Legends|starships]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:N1starfighter-SWCCG.jpg|thumb|left|An N-1 [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] in flight.]]
The Royal N-1 starfighter featured the best elements of Naboo design, being aesthetically sound and adhering to the Naboo's love for curves and aerodynamic shapes.<ref name="CCS" />

A [[Chromium/Legends|chromium]] finish on the front of the vehicle would gleam in the sunlight during parades and celebratory fly-bys. This chromium was purely decorative and reserved for starships serving the [[Royal House of Naboo/Legends|Royal House of Naboo]]. Once, the chromium was used to deflect rays from Naboo's sun, and all starships were fitted with it. The finish contrasted sharply with rest of the N-1, which was yellow in color.<ref name="CCS" />

The citizens of Naboo were dedicated to the defense of their ecologically sensitive [[Planet/Legends|world]], and the N-1 was an example of this commitment. Its specialized engine system, twin [[221 sublight engine|J-type Nubian 221]] sub-light pulse engines, ensured that fuel would burn hotter in order to reduce harmful emissions.<ref name="CCS" />

[[File:N1_ep1ig.png|thumb|left|180px|N-1 schematics.]]

An advanced cooling system which incorporated several heat sinks along the engine finials prevented overheating. The rear finial could be connected to special outlets in the [[Theed Hangar/Legends|Theed Hangar]] to recharge the craft and transmit important data, even coded mission profiles.<ref name="CCS" />

However, it could still perform the tank-buster job in a pinch, as Naboo pilot [[Rhys Dallows]] found when he had to defend a Resistance base hidden in his [[Naboo training canyon|old training canyon]].<ref name="SW:SF">[[Star Wars: Starfighter (video game)|''Star Wars: Starfighter'']]</ref>

In order to accompany the [[Queen/Legends|Queen's]] starship to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] or other distant planets, each N-1 was equipped with a [[Nubia Star Drives, Incorporated/Legends|Nubian]] [[Monarc C-4 hyperdrive/Legends|Monarc C-4]] hyperdrive with a range of 1,000 [[Light-year/Legends|light-years]]. When this was insufficient, the escort fighters could refuel in transit via the [[J-type diplomatic barge/Legends|J-type diplomatic barge's]] under-wing docking sockets.<ref name="CCS" />

[[File:Couplingunit.jpg|thumb|left|An N-1's "tail" docked with a coupling unit for refueling.]]
The pilot was protected by advanced [[Life support/Legends|life support]] systems and [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], aided by an [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] that would help the pilot with repairs and adjustments.<ref name="CCS" />

The N-1 starfighter was also equipped with an advanced [[Autopilot/Legends|autopilot]] that could receive navigational information from hangar outlets or from Naboo flight control. In a crisis, the autopilot could bring the craft to the site of an emergency or pilot the ship home safely.<ref name="CCS" />

The N-1's weapons were twin [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]] and a full complement of 10 [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedoes]]. These were powerful enough to allow the N-1 to engage even the superior numbers of [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|''Vulture'' droids]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|Droid Control Ship]] as was required during the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]].<ref name="CCS" />

==History==
[[File:N1topview.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Top view of an N-1 starfighter.]]
The N-1 entered Naboo service in 33 BBY, replacing its predecessor, the [[N-1L Light Starfighter|N-1L light starfighter]],<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> during [[King/Legends|King]] [[Ars Veruna/Legends|Ars Veruna's]] reign. As the monarch's pet project,<ref name="SWDP" /> the N-1 quickly became the standard starfighter among Naboo pilots.<ref name="SW:GB" />

In [[36 BBY/Legends|36 BBY]], an N-1 was used to seal off a storage area revealed by a beached [[Sando aqua monster/Legends|Sando aqua monster]].<ref name="Monster">{{GamerCite|2|The Monster}}</ref>

[[Agamar/Legends|Agamar]] attempted to acquire N-1 starfigthers. When Naboo refused to sell them, [[Bravo Eight]] [[Dren Melne]] made a deal with the Agamarians so they could capture one. Two [[Carrier/Legends|carriers]] ambushed [[Echo Flight]], but [[Essara Till/Legends|Essara Till]] and the other pilots drove off the attackers, and Melne was killed.<ref name="SF Trap">{{GamerCite|1|The Starfighter Trap}}</ref>

Two Naboo fighters, piloted by Till and rookie Rhys Dallows were [[Attempted kidnapping of Queen Amidala|escorting]] the Queen's cruiser near an asteroid field to preliminary discussions with the Trade Federation when they were ambushed by [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] in various starfighters, including [[MorningStar]]s, [[Dianoga-class assault starfighter|Dianogas]], and [[Dagger-class starfighter|Daggers]]. The two pilots fended off the marauders in their N-1s while the Queen returned to Naboo.<ref name="SW:SF" />

Later, N-1s would be used to resist the Trade Federation [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion of Naboo]], but they were no match for the might of the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]]. However, a [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] of these fighters, [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Flight]], scrambled to attack the Droid Control Ship [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|''Vuutun Palaa'']] over Naboo and shut down the droid army [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|fighting]] the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]]. They were able to penetrate the swarms of droid starfighters and attack the vessel, but even their proton torpedoes could not penetrate the heavy [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]]. Thanks to [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's]] [[Precognition/Legends|accidental]] destruction of some of the ship's reactors from inside the vessel, they were successful.<ref name="SWEI:TPM" />

===Later history===
[[File:N1_fighter.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An N-1 starfighter.]]
The success of the N-1 led to the reputation of starfighters as battleship-killers.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], 30 of these starfighters, along with a corporate [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] loyal to the Galactic Republic, were sent to [[Battle of Lanteeb|rescue]] [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] trapped on [[Lanteeb/Legends|Lanteeb]].<ref name="TCW:Gambit:Siege">''[[Clone Wars Gambit: Siege]]''</ref>

At some point, a quartet of four aged N-1 fighters saw service with the [[Black Hammer pirates]], a [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] group that operated from the planet [[Galantos]] in the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]].<ref name="CATCW">''[[Coruscant and the Core Worlds]]''</ref>

Although their technology was outdated by the time of the post-Clone Wars era,<ref name="Rebel Strike guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> N-1s remained in use for many years, even as late as between [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]] and [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], where several N-1s owned by a Rebel Alliance cell on Naboo were [[Skirmish over Naboo (Galactic Civil War)|used]] against ''Lucrehulk''-class battleships and ''Vulture'' droid fighters sent to Naboo by an unknown party.<ref name="STAC">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref> In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], they flew across the skies of Theed during an [[Rally on Naboo/Legends|uprising]] against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]].<ref name="SWEVI:ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Some were seen in use by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]<ref name="SW:RSII:RL" /> and Rebel sympathizers.<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref>

The Galactic Civil War-era outlaw known as [[Stormtrooper X]] piloted an N-1 christened ''Rogue Imperial 5''.

By [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], the N-1 was described as an 'antique'.<ref name="Tempest">''[[Legacy of the Force: Tempest]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
When R2-D2 successfully overrides the auto pilot on Anakin Skywalker's N-1 during the Battle of Naboo and returns control of the craft to its pilot, the rightmost console panel shows a display nearly identical to those seen on the ''Millennium Falcon''{{'s}} quad laser turrets in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].

Also, the full-size N-1 Starfighter prop used by Anakin Skywalker in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], is on display in the Boston Museum of Science. The museum also had another ''Star Wars'' exhibit, but that was removed sometime in December 2006.

[[Doug Chiang]] has acknowledged that an R2 unit cannot physically exist inside the frame of the spacecraft as it is depicted in Episode I and later in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|Episode II]]. His original concept artwork did allow for the legs of an R2 unit to fit within the tube-shaped socket, but George Lucas directed him to make the socket tube diameter the same, or nearly the same, as the diameter of the droid's head, which does not allow enough room for the legs of the droid. A compromise was reached in the ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Incredible Cross-Sections]]'' book which shows Artoo Detoo collapsing his legs and telescoping his head above his body until it was above the viewing threshold.

N-1 starfighters are unlockable in the [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (series)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] series.

With the introduction of Chapter 8 in ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', the starfighter became a playable ship available to freelance ace [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]]. It was one of several ships made playable in Chapter 8 along with the [[X4 Gunship/Legends|X4 Gunship]], the [[AEG-77 Vigo]], and the [[Ye-4 gunship]].<ref name="Chapter 8">{{SWGWiki|Chapter_8_Notes_for_Jan_15_2008|Chapter 8 Notes for Jan 15 2008}}</ref>
